title: Hypothesis testing: null hypothesis, alternative and significance level

videos.script: Horta switches on a new routing system for its couriers. The supplier promises faster deliveries. Before the switch, deliveries averaged forty minutes. {{before}} After the switch, twenty-five deliveries average thirty-eight point nine. That is faster. Is it the new system, or would twenty-five deliveries under the old one have come out this low anyway? {{question}} Lesson twelve's interval gives part of the answer. This lesson gives the other part a structure that every statistical test follows. {{structure}} It works like a trial. You start by assuming the boring explanation: the new system changed nothing. That is the null hypothesis. {{null}} Then you ask how surprising the data would be if that were true. If it would be very surprising, you reject the boring explanation. If not, you keep it, for now. {{surprise}} Before looking at any data, you decide how surprising is surprising enough. That threshold is the significance level, usually five percent. {{alpha}} By the end you will run a complete test on the twenty-five deliveries, and find out whether the supplier's promise survives it. {{run}}
